answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils with time-locked earned reputation: a new identity starts with zero trust and gains transaction rights by completing useful work over days, each job attested by independent peers. Like basalt cooling into rock, reputation hardens slowly and cannot be rushed; a prism of separate attestations exposes one fake history as contradictions, while a nebula of fresh identities stays dim until each proves itself. An attacker must fund real work and waiting time for every fake, turning a cheap swarm into a costly grind, while one honest agent pays that price only once.
